mainTopic: How עירוב חצרות works (קנייה vs. דירה), then setting one's שבת base (שביתה) from a distance and עירוב with the feet
overview: This amud begins in the middle of a discussion about how an עירוב חצרות works. שמואל says it works through קנייה, and רבה says it works through דירה. The גמרא adds a קטן as another practical difference between them. אביי then challenges both views with a ברייתא in which one person carries the עירוב for five people. רבה answers that the carrier acts as a שליח for all of them. רב then rules that in the earlier three-courtyards case, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. A new משנה follows: a traveler caught by nightfall may set his שבת base at a tree's trunk, but not vaguely 'beneath' it. The משנה also discusses whether the 2000 אמה are measured as a circle or a square, and who may make an עירוב 'with his feet' (רבי מאיר vs. רבי יהודה). The גמרא then asks what 'he has not said anything' means. רב says he loses everything. שמואל says he may reach the tree but must be measured strictly from its far side, like a חמר גמל, so he cannot reach his home.

steps.title: A minor is another practical difference between the two views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its list of practical differences between שמואל and רבה by adding the case of a קטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing an answer that started on the previous amud. It adds one more practical difference between שמואל and רבה: can a קטן collect the עירוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, a עירוב works through קנייה, and a קטן cannot act as a שליח to make an acquisition for others, so his collecting does not work. According to רבה, the food itself creates a shared דירה, so it does not matter who collects it, and a קטן is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor (under בר מצוה age), who cannot legally act as an agent for acquisition
The shared food that joins the residents of a courtyard so they may carry on שבת
Acquisition; שמואל's explanation of how a עירוב works
Residence; רבה's explanation of how a עירוב works

steps.confusionAlert: This one word continues a sentence from the previous section ('the difference between them is... and a minor'). It is not a new topic. It is the last item in a list.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the debate about קנייה vs. דירה is not just theory. It changes who is allowed to set up the עירוב.

phrases.english: And a minor.
phrases.notes: This finishes the list: another practical difference is whether a קטן can collect the עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'מאי בינייהו' (what is the difference between them) answer on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between the קנייה view and the דירה view?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether a קטן can collect the עירוב: invalid according to שמואל (a minor cannot be a שליח for acquisition), valid according to רבה (the food creates residence by itself).

steps.title: אביי challenges both views from the case of five people
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא where one person carries a shared עירוב for five people, and argues that this is hard for both רבה and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: There is a difficulty for you and a difficulty for שמואל. It was taught: Five people who collected their עירוב, when they take it to another place, one person takes it for all of them. But then only he acquires, and nobody else! Only he gets residence, and nobody else!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to challenge both explanations of עירוב at once. If only one person carries the עירוב, it seems only that person should benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five residents of one courtyard combined their food, and now they want to join with another courtyard. The ברייתא says one of them can carry the food there for all five. אביי asks: according to שמואל, only the carrier acquires, and according to רבה, only the carrier gains residence. So how do the other four benefit?

keyTerms.meaning: According to you (your opinion)
It is difficult; a challenge
Collected (the food for the עירוב)
Carries / takes it over
And nobody else / and no more

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabba:
It is difficult for you, and it is difficult for Shmuel.
phrases.notes: One challenge against both the residence view and the acquisition view.

phrases.aramaic: הָא תַּנְיָא: חֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁגָּבוּ אֶת עֵירוּבָן,
phrases.english: For it was taught: five people who collected their eiruv,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהֵם מוֹלִיכִין אֶת עֵירוּבָן לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר —
phrases.english: when they take their eiruv to another place,
phrases.notes: To join with another courtyard.

phrases.english: one person takes it for all of them.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא נִיהוּ דְּקָא קָנֵי, וְתוּ לָא.
phrases.english: It is he who acquires, and nobody else!
phrases.notes: This is the problem for שמואל, who holds the eiruv works by acquiring.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא נִיהוּ דְּקָא דָּיַיר, וְתוּ לָא!
phrases.english: It is he who gains residence, and nobody else!
phrases.notes: This is the problem for רבה, who holds the eiruv works by establishing residence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּה: לְדִידָךְ קַשְׁיָא וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two views and their differences are laid out, אביי attacks both views together.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רבה's דירה view and שמואל's קנייה view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the עירוב works through each person's own acquisition or residence, then the one person who carries it should be the only one to benefit. Yet the ברייתא says it works for all five.

steps.title: רבה answers that the carrier acts as everyone's agent
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the challenge is not a problem for either view, because the one who carries the עירוב is a שליח for all five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: It is not difficult for me, and not difficult for שמואל. He is acting as the agent of all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends both views at once. The carrier is not acting only for himself. He is acting on behalf of everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of שליחות, whatever the carrier does counts for all five. According to שמואל, he acquires for all of them. According to רבה, he sets up residence for all of them. The ברייתא therefore fits both views.

keyTerms.meaning: According to me (my opinion)
Agency; acting legally on someone else's behalf
Does / performs

steps.whatToRemember: One person may carry a shared עירוב for a whole group because he acts as their שליח. This works whether a עירוב is based on קנייה or on דירה.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא, וְלָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: It is not difficult for me, and it is not difficult for Shmuel,
he is performing the agency of all of them.
phrases.notes: The carrier acquires or establishes residence on behalf of everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא, וְלָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל קַשְׁיָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the case: the carrier acts as a שליח, not only for himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one who carries the עירוב acquires or resides only for himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: He acts as the שליח of all five, so all of them acquire or gain residence through him.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון in the three courtyards case
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of tradition, רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the earlier case of three courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said that רב חמא בר גוריא said that רב said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier case of three courtyards, where the middle one made a עירוב with each outer one, and gives the final ruling. The ruling follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון held that one may carry between the middle courtyard and each outer courtyard, in both directions. However, one may not carry from one outer courtyard to the other. This ruling closes that earlier topic with a practical הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
The middle courtyard, between the two outer ones

steps.confusionAlert: This ruling is not about the five people or the קטן discussed just before. It goes back to the three-courtyards case discussed earlier on the daf.
steps.whatToRemember: In the three-courtyards case, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. Carrying is allowed between the middle courtyard and each outer one, but not between the two outer courtyards.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical ruling for how far a עירוב reaches when courtyards are joined in a chain.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: Refers back to the case of three courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the קנייה/דירה discussion and returns to the earlier three-courtyards case to give the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: the middle courtyard may carry to and from each outer courtyard, but the two outer courtyards may not carry to each other.

steps.title: Saying 'my residence is beneath the tree' accomplishes nothing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with a traveler caught by nightfall. He tries to set his שביתה 'beneath' a tree or fence he recognizes, but that statement has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone was traveling, and it got dark (שבת began). He recognized a tree or a fence ahead, and he said, 'My שבת residence is beneath it.' He has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. A traveler tries to set his שבת home base at a tree, but because he said 'beneath it,' the statement does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person's שביתה is where he is when שבת begins. He may instead set it up to 2000 אמה away by naming a specific spot. 'Beneath the tree' covers a wide area, not one precise spot, so the statement does not work as he intended. The גמרא will dispute exactly what he loses.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the core text the גמרא will discuss)
שבת residence or home base; your 2000 אמה are measured from here
It got dark on him, meaning שבת began while he was traveling
A tree or a fence, used as a landmark
He said nothing, meaning the statement has no legal effect

steps.confusionAlert: What 'he said nothing' means in practice is not obvious, and the גמרא brings a מחלוקת about it (steps 13–14). According to רב, he has no valid base at all, so he cannot even go to the tree. According to שמואל, he cannot reach his home, but he may still go to the tree.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who was coming along the road, and it grew dark on him,
phrases.notes: שבת started while he was still traveling.

phrases.english: and he recognized a tree or a fence,
phrases.notes: The landmark is 2000 אמה from him and 2000 אמה from his house.

phrases.english: and he said: 'My residence is beneath it' —
he has not said anything.
phrases.notes: The location is too vague.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier discussion of shared עירובין and three courtyards has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting שביתה 'beneath' a landmark is too vague and has no effect.

steps.title: Saying 'at its trunk' works and allows walking 4000 cubits
steps.stepSummary: If he names the tree's trunk, a precise spot, his שביתה takes effect there. He may then walk 2000 אמה to it and 2000 more beyond it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'My residence is at its trunk,' he may walk from where he is standing to the trunk, 2000 אמה. Then from the trunk to his house, another 2000 אמה. So after dark he ends up walking 4000 אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the case that works. Naming the trunk gives a precise spot, so his שבת home base moves there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trunk is a specific, small point, unlike the vague area 'beneath' the tree. Since his שביתה is now at the trunk, his 2000 אמה limit is measured from the trunk. That is why he gains 2000 אמה past it and can reach his house.

keyTerms.meaning: Its trunk or base, a precise spot
The place where his feet are, where he is standing now
2000 cubits, the שבת walking limit (תחום שבת)
It turns out, the result is

steps.confusionAlert: He is not getting a bigger limit than normal. His 2000 אמה limit simply moved to the trunk. The first 2000 is just the walk to reach his new home base.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a person can set his שביתה from a distance by speaking, as long as he names a precise spot. The גמרא will build on this idea.

phrases.english: If he said 'My residence is at its trunk' —
he may walk from the place of his feet
until its trunk, two thousand cubits,
and from its trunk until his house, two thousand cubits.
It turns out he walks, from when it grew dark,
four thousand cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 5. A precise spot (the trunk) works, while the vague 'beneath' did not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Naming the trunk creates שביתה there, allowing 2000 אמה to it and 2000 אמה beyond it, for 4000 in total.

steps.title: Without a known landmark, his residence is where he stands
steps.stepSummary: If he knows no landmark, or doesn't know this הלכה, and says 'my residence is in my place,' he gets 2000 אמה in every direction from where he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he doesn't recognize any landmark, or he isn't an expert in the הלכה, and he says 'My residence is in my place,' then his spot gives him 2000 אמה in every direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the default case. When the traveler can't, or doesn't know how to, set his שביתה elsewhere, his home base is the spot where he stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no distant spot is named, so his שביתה stays at his own location. This gives him 2000 אמה in all directions, but it may not get him home.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert in the הלכה (here, someone who knows a שביתה can be set from a distance)
In my place, where I am standing
His place acquires for him, meaning his spot becomes his home base
In every direction

phrases.english: If he does not recognize a landmark,
or he is not an expert in the halakha,
and he said 'My residence is in my place' —
his place acquires for him
two thousand cubits in every direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ מַכִּיר אוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי בַּהֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fallback case when the landmark method of step 6 is not available.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a named landmark, his current spot is his שביתה, giving 2000 אמה in every direction.

steps.title: Dispute: are the 2000 cubits measured as a circle or a square
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says the 2000 אמה form a circle. חכמים say they form a square, so the person gains the extra distance in the corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 2000 אמה are measured in a circle, according to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. חכמים say they are measured as a square, like a square tablet, so that he gains the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a dispute about the shape of the 2000 אמה area around a person's שביתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a circle, every point at the edge is exactly 2000 אמה from the center. In a square with 4000 אמה sides, the corners stretch out to about 2800 אמה from the center. That is the extra space חכמים give him.

keyTerms.meaning: Circular, measured as a circle
Square, measured as a square
A tablet or board
He gains the corners

steps.whatToRemember: A precise named spot moves your שביתה, and a vague area does not. Without a landmark, your spot is your base. The 2000 אמה area is a circle according to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס and a square, including the corners, according to חכמים.

phrases.english: Circular,
the words of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigenos;
and the Sages say: square,
like a square tablet,
so that he gains the corners.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲגוּלּוֹת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the '2000 אמה in every direction' from step 7 is actually measured.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Circle according to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס. Square including the corners according to חכמים.

steps.title: This is what is meant by 'the poor man makes an עירוב with his feet'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a name to the traveler's method: setting a שביתה by being there or declaring it in person, without bread, is called 'עני מערב ברגליו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what חכמים meant when they said: the poor man makes his עירוב with his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ties the earlier traveler cases to a well-known saying. Setting a שביתה in person, without food, is called 'making an עירוב with one's feet.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב תחומין is normally made by placing bread at a spot. This line teaches that a person can also set his שביתה simply by being somewhere, or by naming a precise nearby spot. That method is called 'with his feet,' and it is linked to the עני, the person who has no bread to use.

keyTerms.meaning: A method of moving one's שבת base point so the 2000 אמה are measured from a new spot
Makes an עירוב with his feet, meaning in person and without bread
A poor person; here, one who has no bread for an עירוב

steps.confusionAlert: 'וזו היא שאמרו' does not open a new case. It points back to the traveler of steps 5–7 and tells you that his method is the famous 'עירוב with the feet.'

phrases.english: And this is what they (the Sages) said:
phrases.notes: Points back to the traveler cases just described

phrases.english: The poor man makes an eruv with his feet.
phrases.notes: He sets his base by being there in person, not with bread

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Labels the method used in the traveler cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting a שביתה in person without bread is called 'עירוב with the feet' and is linked to the עני.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: only a poor person may use the feet method
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר limits the 'feet' method to someone who has no bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: we only allow this for a poor person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר rules that only an עני may set his שביתה with his feet. Someone who has bread must make his עירוב with bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the feet method is a fallback for someone who cannot do the normal method. If you have bread, the bread עירוב is the required way.

keyTerms.meaning: We have only, meaning this applies only to

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
We have (this rule) only for a poor man.
phrases.notes: A rich person must use bread

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits who may use the method from step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one without bread may make an עירוב with his feet.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: rich and poor alike may use the feet method
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the feet method is the basic way for everyone. Bread was allowed only as a convenience for the rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a poor person and a rich person are the same. חכמים allowed an עירוב with bread only to make things easier for the rich person, so he would not have to go out and make the עירוב with his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר. Anyone may set his שביתה with his feet, and bread is just an easier extra option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reverses רבי מאיר's picture. For him, going in person is the basic method. Bread is a leniency so a wealthy person can send someone else with bread instead of walking there himself. Having bread therefore never takes away the feet option.

keyTerms.meaning: A rich person; here, one who has bread
Bread, the food normally used for an עירוב
To make it easier; to be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds that the feet method is only for one without bread. רבי יהודה holds that the feet method is for everyone, and bread is only a convenience.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Both a poor man and a rich man (may do it);
They did not say that one makes an eruv with bread
phrases.notes: The bread method was not meant to replace the feet method

phrases.english: except to make it easier for the rich man,
so that he need not go out and make an eruv with his feet.
phrases.notes: He can send bread with someone else instead

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד עָנִי וְאֶחָד עָשִׁיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may make an עירוב with his feet; bread is a leniency for the wealthy.

steps.title: What does 'he has not said anything' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far the failure goes in the case of 'beneath the tree' (step 5).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'he has not said anything' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to the vague 'beneath the tree' case from step 5. It asks what the משנה's words 'he has not said anything' actually mean. This question sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the vague statement has no effect, but it did not say what this means in practice. It could mean he loses everything, even the area near where he stands. Or it could mean he only fails to gain the extra distance he wanted.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
He has not said anything, meaning his statement has no effect

phrases.english: GEMARA: What does 'he has not said anything' mean?
phrases.notes: Refers to the vague 'beneath the tree' case

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by returning to the case in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far the 'no effect' ruling goes: does he lose everything, or only the distance beyond the tree?

steps.title: רב: the statement fails completely, so he cannot even reach the tree
steps.stepSummary: רב says the person has no valid base at all, so he cannot even go to the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: he has said nothing at all, so he cannot even go to the spot beneath the tree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the vague statement wipes out everything. The person cannot even walk to the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His statement was too vague to set his base at the tree. But by trying to move it there, he also gave up his base where he stands. He is left with almost no movement: only four אמות from where he is standing.

keyTerms.meaning: At all; completely
To the area beneath the tree
Is able to go

phrases.english: Rav said:
He has not said anything at all,
for even to beneath the tree
he is not able to go.
phrases.notes: He lost both the tree and his current spot as a base

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם כׇּל עִיקָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement fails completely; he cannot even go to the tree.

steps.title: שמואל: he cannot reach his home, but he may go to the tree
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the failure is only about going further, to his home. He may still go to the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: he has said nothing regarding getting to his home, but he may go to the spot beneath the tree.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a narrower answer than רב. The person loses only the extra distance, the 2000 אמה past the tree toward his home. He may still walk to the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the statement does create a base somewhere under the tree, but we do not know exactly where. So he may go to the tree, as long as the whole area under it is within 2000 אמה of him. But his limit beyond the tree must be measured strictly, as steps 15–16 explain, so he cannot count on reaching his house.

keyTerms.meaning: To his home

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement fails only for reaching home; he may still go to the tree.

steps.title: The area under the tree becomes a 'donkey driver and camel driver' case
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains why the person cannot reach his home. His base could be anywhere under the tree, so he is pulled in two directions, like a חמר גמל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the area beneath the tree becomes like a donkey driver and a camel driver, pulled from both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues שמואל's answer from step 14. It explains why the person may go to the tree but may not go further to his home. This also sets up the measuring rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person said "beneath the tree" but never picked one exact spot. His base could be anywhere in that area, so we do not know where it is. A חמר גמל leads a camel from the front and drives a donkey from behind, so he is pulled both ways. In the same way, the doubt pulls this person's base toward both sides of the tree.

keyTerms.meaning: A donkey driver and camel driver. He is pulled in two opposite directions, so he is stuck. The phrase is used for a case of double doubt that leads to strictness both ways.
Beneath the tree. This is the area he named as his base without picking an exact spot.
And it becomes.

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is NOT saying the person has no base. That was רב's view in step 13. שמואל says he does have a base under the tree. We just do not know exactly where it is, so we are strict on every side.

phrases.english: And the area beneath the tree becomes
phrases.notes: Continuation of שמואל's explanation

phrases.english: a donkey driver and camel driver (pulled from both sides).
phrases.notes: A donkey driver walks behind his animal and a camel driver in front of his, so he's pulled in opposite directions.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַעֲשֶׂה תַּחְתָּיו שֶׁל אִילָן חַמָּר גַּמָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind שמואל's position in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far does the failure go when someone sets his base 'beneath the tree' without naming a spot? (asked in step 12)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His base is somewhere under the tree but uncertain, so he is pulled both ways (חמר גמל).

steps.title: Measuring strictly from the opposite side of the tree
steps.stepSummary: Because of the doubt, his 2000 אמה limit is measured from the far edge of the tree. If he wants to go north, we measure from the south. If he wants to go south, we measure from the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he comes to measure from the north, we measure for him from the south. If he comes to measure from the south, we measure for him from the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the practical result of the חמר גמל idea. It tells us exactly how to measure this person's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His base could be at any point under the tree. Suppose he wants to walk north. Maybe his real base is the southern end, which gives him the least distance northward. So we measure from the south edge. The same logic works in reverse for walking south. This is why his home, which lies past that strict limit, stays out of reach.

keyTerms.meaning: To measure (his allowed distance)
We measure for him (the court measures)
North
South

steps.whatToRemember: רב says this person has no base at all, so he cannot even go to the tree. שמואל says he has a base somewhere under the tree. Because we do not know where, we measure strictly from the opposite edge in each direction. That keeps him from reaching his home.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of a doubt that makes us strict in both directions (חמר גמל). The same idea comes up in many places in הלכה.
